Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

Kelby Hammer confirmed on 09/23/2026 that flagging these is correct and that it is a training point: technicians should select stop-work authority only when it was actually used, and may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose. These are listed for the technician to confirm, not as confirmed events. "Stop work authority utilized" was not selected on any form today. Where stop-work appears at all, it is the routine pre-job item "Stop work authority was discussed".
"Unsafe conditions" selected with no narrative describing an unsafe condition:

Jeremy Norris — XTO, McClintic J #33, job 36470_1, 7:27 PM. Selected "Unsafe conditions" alongside "Stop work authority was discussed". The narrative reads "A great meeting between all to discuss the LMRAs and LSRAs as they pertain to this job and exactly what our ERP would be in case of emergency" — it describes a pre-job briefing, not a condition. That identical string also appears on his Trinity 37 #2 (36167) and Stephens A #3 (36169) forms today, which indicates text and selections being carried forward rather than made fresh.

Tyrell Sanders — XTO, Kyle 2600 Unit 1 2621SH, job 36372, second OWL at 1:50 PM. Selected "Unsafe conditions"; the narrative reads only "Lockout tag out", which names a control measure rather than a condition. Neither stop-work item was selected.

Ruben Rojo — XTO, Baumann 16 #9, job 36161, 12:09 PM. Selected "Unsafe conditions"; the narrative reads only "Packing replacement on wellhead". The what-went-well note says "No dangerous materials or gas on break", which does not support an unsafe condition. Neither stop-work item was selected.

Not the mis-selection pattern — Raymundo Solis, XTO Kyle 2600 Unit 1 2621SH, job 36371, 2:09 PM. Solis also selected "Unsafe conditions", but his narrative names a real hazard and the response to it: "Unsafe conditions was talked about due to the weather. We mentioned that if it starts to rain and lightning we will stop the job and waited out to see if it passes." This is a correctly documented weather hazard with a stated stop trigger. It should not be grouped with the three above, and no follow-up is needed beyond noting it was done properly.

The inverse — two forms name a real condition without selecting "Unsafe conditions". 1099 Gael Antonio Avila, XTO McClintic J #33, job 36470_2, 6:17 PM, recorded "Quick check on a leaking valve" with no unsafe-conditions selection, no further detail, and an entirely blank close-out. Michael Jobe, XTO Brook D 17H-HDR, job 36420_1, 2:06 PM, recorded "The vac truck I noticed was not sucking so I told the guy that something is wrong was on standby till another truck got here" — an equipment failure he raised and that put the crew on standby, with no unsafe-conditions selection. Jobe's entry reads as the technician doing the right thing and documenting it; the selection simply does not reflect it. Avila's leaking valve is the one worth a direct question.

Technicians on this list on previous days: Nathan Contreras appeared on the stop-work confirmation list on 09/23 and again on 09/26. Today he selected no stop-work or unsafe-conditions item on either of his two air jobs. Michael Jobe selected "Unsafe conditions" twice in one day on 09/26 with no supporting narrative; today he did not select it and gave a substantive narrative instead.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review, because only the text of each form is read. In particular, fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates, and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images and not as text fields, so none of those can be checked here. Alexander Clubb's "No tag" entry on trailer 507 is an example of a condition that only became visible because a technician happened to type it.

85 of 85 submissions read. The job board was available: Blake Walton's 10/29/2026 email arrived at 10:15 AM Central with both workbooks, and the 10-29 sheet of each was used. 55 manned board rows were checked for coverage — 44 on the Permian Basin board and 11 on the ArkLaTex board — excluding rows marked CANCELLED, ON STANDBY, DAYS OFF, WTX SUPPORT and SHOP. Because this review ran at 11:00 PM Central on the day itself, the usual second search over the following morning for late-arriving submissions could not be run; any form for 10/29 that lands after midnight is not included here.
